text:
The Lightning were down 3-1 midway through the third period, and by the time Nikita Kucherov won it in overtime, the Wild's three-game winning streak was gone. Tampa Bay came back from two goals down to beat Minnesota 4-3 at Grand Casino Arena. Kucherov's power-play wrist shot at 3:23 of the extra period capped it, and Brayden Point reached 700 career points along the way with two assists.

Minnesota's lead came early and cheaply. Blake Coleman scored at 0:55 of the first, and Maxim Shabanov, a free agent who was never drafted and arrived from Traktor Chelyabinsk of the KHL, added a power-play goal before the three-minute mark. He scored again in the third to make it 3-1. But the Lightning controlled the game. They outshot Minnesota 34-22, put up 83 shot attempts to 42, and won the expected goals count, which measures the quality of chances, 4.12 to 1.96. By our simulation of every shot, TBL deserved to win 82 percent of the time. Jake Guentzel scored twice, including a tip-in at 13:44 of the third, and Charle-Edouard D'Astous tied it on a power-play slap shot at 16:29.

The power play was the gap between the two sides. Tampa Bay went 3 for 6 with the man advantage, while Minnesota blocked 22 shots to the Lightning's 10 and still could not keep the puck out. Calvin Pickard stopped 30 of 34 and finished almost exactly where the chances said he should. The Lightning have now won three straight. The Wild, who took the October meeting 2-3 in regulation against the same opponent, have to start a new run, and we'd watch whether they can hold a lead when the play is going the other way.
